reason: SARIF publishes one rule descriptor per channel, deduplicated per run, so collapsing three level pairs into three channels removes three descriptors from tool.driver.rules and renumbers every result's ruleIndex. Structural, not a rename: a map row substitutes a name inside a value, and this is a table losing rows. Nothing else in the artifact moved — the findings, their ids, their fingerprints and every other surface of this case are equal under the ten declared rows.

The same structural shift for the two coupling channels: two fewer descriptors in tool.driver.rules and the resulting ruleIndex renumbering. The descriptor text is the producing rule's own description, which never carried a level, so the surviving descriptors are byte-identical to the ones the reference published for the .class half.
